program: Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering
source_note: This file carries only the analysis knowledge layer. Every CLO, Student Outcome, Performance Indicator, course, teaching strategy and assessment method is read from data/ee_curriculum.json, and the program assessment cycle is read from data/ee-assessment.json. No outcome definition or approved mapping is duplicated here. Program-level conclusions are computed from required (core) courses only; the required/elective classification is read from curriculum.courses[].required_or_elective.

philosophy.headline: Supportive review, not audit
philosophy.statement: CLO-SO-PI alignment is a matter of faculty judgment. This analysis assumes the approved mapping is intentional and potentially defensible, and looks first for the strongest reasonable interpretation that supports it.
order_of_preference: Preserve the approved mapping wherever a reasonable interpretation supports it.
Strengthen the assessment evidence so the mapping becomes visible in student work.
Clarify the rationale or the rubric criterion so the intent is explicit.
Consider remapping only where there is a strong and specific conceptual mismatch.
philosophy.authority_note: Faculty judgment remains authoritative. Nothing on this page changes an approved mapping; the page produces discussion material for the curriculum and assessment committees.

layers.name: Alignment Layer
layers.description: Approved curriculum mappings between course learning outcomes, ABET Student Outcomes and program Performance Indicators.

layers.name: Evidence Layer
layers.source: Approved assessment-method pool in data/ee_curriculum.json plus the recommendation model in this file
layers.description: Assessment artifacts and rubric criteria that could carry the evidence for each mapping. Where no artifact has been linked yet, the page shows the recommended evidence type instead of inventing one.

layers.name: Measurement Layer
layers.description: Scored student work and computed attainment. No student performance or attainment value is stored, derived or displayed in this release.

layers.name: Improvement Layer
layers.description: Assessment findings, improvement actions and reassessment outcomes. Reserved for a later release.

well_supported.label: Well Supported
well_supported.definition: The outcome statement calls for the same kind of demonstration the Performance Indicator describes, and the declared assessment methods already include an artifact type that can carry that evidence.
well_supported.lead_phrase: This mapping appears well supported because

defensible.label: Defensible
defensible.definition: A reasonable interpretation supports the mapping. It holds provided the assessed task makes the indicator's demonstration visible in student work.
defensible.lead_phrase: This mapping is defensible provided that

could_be_strengthened.label: Could Be Strengthened
could_be_strengthened.definition: The mapping is retained. The evidence that would demonstrate it is thinner than it could be, so an added artifact, a clearer rubric criterion or a short written rationale would make it easier to defend.
could_be_strengthened.lead_phrase: The relationship could be strengthened by

review_recommended.label: Review Recommended
review_recommended.definition: Reserved for a strong and specific conceptual difference between what the outcome statement describes and what the indicator measures. Even here the preserve path comes first: if the assessed task carries the indicator's demonstration, clarified wording or a named rubric criterion is enough.
review_recommended.lead_phrase: A change may be worth considering only if

foundational_knowledge.label: foundational knowledge
foundational_knowledge.description: Recalling, defining or describing established principles, components and representations.

analysis.label: engineering analysis
analysis.description: Formulating, modelling, computing, solving and interpreting engineering problems.

design.label: engineering design
design.description: Devising, developing, implementing or realising a component, system or process against stated needs.

communication.label: technical communication
communication.description: Conveying engineering information in written, oral, visual or graphical form for an intended audience.

ethics.label: ethical judgment
ethics.description: Recognising professional or ethical responsibility and weighing the wider impact of engineering decisions.

teamwork.label: teamwork
teamwork.description: Contributing to a team, planning shared work, or supporting a collaborative and inclusive environment.

experimentation.label: experimentation
experimentation.description: Developing or running experiments, collecting measurements, and drawing conclusions from data.

knowledge_acquisition.label: self-directed learning
knowledge_acquisition.description: Acquiring new knowledge, tools or standards independently and putting them to use.

exam_item.label: Targeted exam or quiz item
exam_item.description: One or more identified questions on a major, final or quiz paper, scored against a published answer key or item rubric. Isolates a single indicator well; needs an open-ended item to reach design, judgment or communication indicators.

homework.label: Homework or classwork assignment
homework.description: Assigned problem work. Useful as supporting evidence; usually needs a nominated question set and a scoring key before it becomes attainment evidence.

simulation_assignment.label: Simulation or computational assignment
simulation_assignment.description: Modelling, coding or simulation work submitted with results. Carries formulation, solution and data-interpretation evidence well.

lab_practical.label: Laboratory practical assessment
lab_practical.description: Observed bench or hardware performance, scored while the student works. Strong for conducting experimentation and for observed team behaviour.

lab_report.label: Laboratory report
lab_report.description: Written account of an experiment with data, analysis and conclusions. Carries data-analysis and engineering-judgment evidence.

design_project.label: Design project or design assignment
design_project.description: Open-ended design work against stated needs and constraints. The natural home for design, constraint and standards evidence; needs a criterion-level rubric to isolate individual indicators.

written_report.label: Technical report
written_report.description: Proposal, interim or final report. Flexible carrier for communication, judgment, standards and self-directed-learning evidence when the rubric names the criterion.

oral_presentation.label: Oral or technical presentation
oral_presentation.description: Presented and questioned in front of an audience. The most direct carrier for audience-adaptation and oral communication evidence.

demonstration.label: Prototype or system demonstration
demonstration.description: A working artifact shown and tested. Evidences realisation of a design and application of newly acquired tools.

peer_team_assessment.label: Teamwork or peer assessment instrument
peer_team_assessment.description: Structured peer or instructor rating of observed team behaviour against named criteria. The standard carrier for teamwork and leadership indicators.

progress_assessment.label: Weekly or milestone progress assessment
progress_assessment.description: Recurring supervisor judgment against milestones. Evidences planning, task management and reliable contribution over time.

employer_assessment.label: Employer or site-supervisor evaluation
employer_assessment.description: Third-party rating of workplace performance. Valuable corroborating evidence; programs differ on whether it is counted as direct, so record the classification decision alongside it.

indirect_survey.label: Course exit survey or other indirect instrument
indirect_survey.description: Student self-report. Supports and contextualises direct evidence; it is not a substitute for it.

Major and Final Exams.note: Nominate the specific questions that carry the indicator rather than using the whole paper score.

Quizzes.note: Short and frequent; strongest as supporting evidence or as an early checkpoint.

Homework and Classwork Assignments.note: Nominate a specific assignment and scoring key if this is to serve as attainment evidence.

Simulation/Computational Assignments.note: Collect the submitted model or code alongside the result so the reasoning is inspectable.

Laboratory Practical Assessment.note: Scored during the session; keep the observation sheet as the evidence record.

Laboratory Reports.note: Separate the data-handling criterion from the write-up criterion so two indicators do not share one score.

Design Project Assignment.note: Use criterion-level rubric rows so individual design indicators can be reported separately.

Written Reports (Proposal, Interim, and.note: Stage-specific rubric rows let different indicators be measured at different points.

Final Report.note: Name which report sections carry each indicator.

Oral Presentations.note: Include a question-and-answer criterion if audience adaptation is being measured.

Oral Technical Presentation.note: Include a question-and-answer criterion if audience adaptation is being measured.

Final Oral Presentation.note: Often the only place where audience adaptation is directly observable.

Prototype/System Demonstration.note: Record the acceptance test used so the demonstration is repeatable evidence.

Teamwork/Peer Assessment.note: Use behaviour-anchored criteria rather than a single overall rating.

Weekly Progress Assessment.note: Aggregate milestone judgments rather than attendance.

Employer Assessment.note: Record how the program classifies this instrument before using it for attainment.

evidence_quality_dimensions.label: Directly measures the intended skill
evidence_quality_dimensions.question: Does the artifact require the student to perform the demonstration the indicator describes, rather than to report or recall it?
evidence_quality_dimensions.guidance: Direct student work outweighs self-report. Where the only available evidence is indirect, pair it with at least one direct artifact.

evidence_quality_dimensions.label: Sufficiently challenging
evidence_quality_dimensions.question: Is the task demanding enough that a passing score means the indicator was genuinely met?
evidence_quality_dimensions.guidance: Recall-level items rarely evidence design, judgment or experimentation indicators, however carefully they are scored.

evidence_quality_dimensions.label: Has a clear rubric
evidence_quality_dimensions.question: Is there a published criterion with performance levels that a second grader could apply consistently?
evidence_quality_dimensions.guidance: Indicators carrying an ABET rubric flag in the program framework should be evidenced by a rubric-bearing artifact.

evidence_quality_dimensions.label: Isolates the indicator being measured
evidence_quality_dimensions.question: Can the score for this indicator be separated from the scores for everything else in the same task?
evidence_quality_dimensions.guidance: A single overall project mark cannot report several indicators separately. Criterion-level rubric rows solve this.

evidence_quality_dimensions.label: Produces defensible attainment evidence
evidence_quality_dimensions.question: Could the artifact, its rubric and its scores be shown to an external reviewer as the basis for the reported attainment?
evidence_quality_dimensions.guidance: Keep the artifact, the rubric, the scoring records and the sample definition together.

notes.broad: This outcome is touched across a wide part of the required curriculum, so every student meets it in several courses.
notes.moderate: This outcome is carried by a meaningful subset of the required curriculum.
notes.focused: This outcome is carried by a small set of required courses. That can be entirely intentional for a specialised outcome; the point worth confirming is that the chosen courses are the ones the program wants to assess.

concentration.note: A large share of this outcome’s CLO to PI relationships sits in a few required courses. This measures where the mapped relationships are declared, not how much time students spend on the outcome. Concentration is normal for capstone-anchored and integrative outcomes; the point worth confirming is that the assessment plan does not depend on a single course offering.

coverage_model.threshold_note: Coverage categories and advisory thresholds are descriptive curriculum-analysis settings chosen for this portal. They are not ABET requirements, accreditation criteria or attainment thresholds, and they can be changed in data/ee_alignment_evidence.json without altering any approved mapping.

evidence_readiness.note: Share of an outcome’s relationships for which an artifact type normally used to report the indicator is already among the declared assessment methods.

PI11.demonstrates: the student separates a problem into its requirements, interacting variables and technical issues before attempting a solution
PI11.relationship: Problem framing is the entry point of SO1: a student who cannot name the requirements and the interacting variables cannot formulate or solve the problem that follows.
strengthening: Use an item or task that presents an under-specified situation, so identifying the requirements is the work rather than a given.
Ask for the interacting variables and the technical issues explicitly, as a named deliverable rather than as an implied first step.
rubric_criteria: Identifies the governing requirements and constraints of the problem completely and accurately.
Names the interacting variables and the technical issues that make the problem non-routine.
PI11.attainment_methodology: Percentage of assessed students reaching a faculty-defined rubric level on the problem-framing criterion of the nominated artifact.
PI11.evidence_note: This indicator carries an ABET rubric in the program framework, so a rubric-bearing artifact is preferred over a raw exam score.

PI12.demonstrates: the student converts a described situation into an engineering or mathematical model with stated assumptions, parameters and governing relationships
PI12.relationship: Modelling is the bridge in SO1 between the identified problem and the applied engineering, science and mathematics that solve it.
strengthening: Score the stated assumptions and the chosen parameters as their own criterion, not only the final model.
Use at least one item where the model is not supplied, so formulating it is what is being measured.
rubric_criteria: States assumptions and parameters that are appropriate and sufficient for the situation.
Produces a governing model that correctly represents the described system.
PI12.attainment_methodology: Average score on the model-formulation criterion across the nominated items, reported with the percentage of students at or above the defined threshold.
PI12.evidence_note: Well carried by mid-level analysis courses; a model supplied inside the question removes the evidence.

PI13.demonstrates: the student carries the formulated problem through to a correct solution using analytical, computational or experimental methods
PI13.relationship: This is the closing step of SO1 and the indicator most course work naturally produces, which is why its evidence is usually plentiful and its rubric is usually a scoring key.
strengthening: Nominate specific questions rather than the whole paper, so the reported attainment maps to this indicator alone.
Where the method is chosen by the student, score the appropriateness of the chosen method as well as the numerical result.
rubric_criteria: Selects an appropriate analytical, computational or experimental method for the formulated problem.
Executes the method correctly and arrives at a defensible result.
PI13.attainment_methodology: Percentage of assessed students scoring at or above the defined threshold on the nominated solution items.
PI13.evidence_note: The most heavily used indicator in the program; the risk here is dilution across too many items rather than lack of evidence.

PI21.demonstrates: the student applies a design process to produce a solution that satisfies a stated need
PI21.relationship: PI21 is the core of SO2: the presence of a specified need and a produced solution is what separates design evidence from analysis evidence.
strengthening: Make the specification explicit in the task statement, so the solution can be judged against a stated need rather than against a model answer.
Where the course work is analytical, frame at least one task as selecting or sizing a configuration to meet given specifications; that turns analysis work into design evidence.
rubric_criteria: Produces a solution that meets the stated specification.
Shows a design process: requirements, candidate solutions, selection and verification against the specification.
PI21.attainment_methodology: Percentage of assessed students meeting the defined rubric level on the design-outcome criterion of the nominated project or demonstration.
PI21.evidence_note: This indicator carries an ABET rubric in the program framework.

PI22.demonstrates: the student's design accounts for public health, safety and welfare together with global, cultural, social, environmental and economic factors
PI22.relationship: SO2 asks for more than a working solution; PI22 is where the wider consideration is evidenced, and it is most visible when those factors are a scored part of the deliverable.
strengthening: Require a named section or rubric row in which the relevant factors are identified and their influence on the design decision is explained.
Ask which factors were considered and set aside, and why; that produces stronger evidence than a checklist.
rubric_criteria: Identifies the health, safety, welfare, societal, environmental and economic factors relevant to this design.
Explains how the identified factors changed or constrained the design decision.
PI22.attainment_methodology: Percentage of assessed students meeting the defined rubric level on the broader-factors criterion.
PI22.evidence_note: This indicator carries an ABET rubric in the program framework.

PI23.demonstrates: the student identifies realistic constraints on the design and justifies why they apply
PI23.relationship: Constraints are what make a design problem realistic; PI23 evidences that the student can name them and defend their relevance rather than accept a supplied list.
strengthening: Ask students to state the constraints themselves and justify each one, instead of supplying the constraint list in the task.
Score justification separately from identification.
rubric_criteria: Identifies constraints that are realistic and relevant to this specific design.
Justifies each constraint with reference to the application context.
PI23.attainment_methodology: Percentage of assessed students meeting the defined rubric level on the constraint-identification and justification criterion.
PI23.evidence_note: This indicator carries an ABET rubric in the program framework.

PI24.demonstrates: the student locates the applicable engineering standards and codes and applies them in the design
PI24.relationship: Standards work anchors SO2 in professional practice; the evidence is strongest when a named standard visibly changes a design decision.
strengthening: Require the specific standard or code clause to be cited, not the standards body alone.
Score whether the cited standard actually governs the decision it is attached to.
rubric_criteria: Cites engineering standards or codes that genuinely apply to the design.
Applies the cited requirement correctly in the design decision.
PI24.attainment_methodology: Percentage of assessed students meeting the defined rubric level on the standards-and-codes criterion.
PI24.evidence_note: This indicator carries an ABET rubric in the program framework. Where a course is analysis-led, a single standards-referenced task can carry it well.

PI31.demonstrates: the student conveys engineering information that is relevant, accurate and sufficient for the purpose
PI31.relationship: PI31 is the substance half of SO3: correct and complete technical content, independently of how well it is delivered.
strengthening: Score technical accuracy and sufficiency as a criterion distinct from delivery and format.
Keep the graded communication artifact, not only the mark, as the evidence record.
rubric_criteria: Presents technically accurate engineering information.
Includes the information the audience needs, without material omissions or padding.
PI31.attainment_methodology: Percentage of assessed students meeting the defined rubric level on the content-accuracy and sufficiency criterion.
PI31.evidence_note: This indicator carries an ABET rubric in the program framework.

PI32.demonstrates: the student chooses the communication method and the engineering representation that fit the message
PI32.relationship: SO3 expects fluency with the discipline's representations, so PI32 is evidenced by schematics, plots, block diagrams and drawings as much as by prose.
strengthening: Include a rubric row on the correctness and readability of figures, schematics and plots.
Ask for the same result in two representations so the choice itself becomes visible.
rubric_criteria: Selects communication methods and engineering representations appropriate to the message.
Produces figures, schematics or plots that are correct, labelled and readable.
PI32.attainment_methodology: Average rubric score on the representation criterion, reported with the percentage of students at or above the defined threshold.
PI32.evidence_note: Often already present in report and presentation rubrics under a general presentation-quality heading; naming it separately makes it reportable.

PI33.demonstrates: the student adjusts depth, terminology and framing to suit a particular audience
PI33.relationship: This is the part of SO3 that the words "a range of audiences" add; it needs a task where the audience is specified or varies.
strengthening: Name the audience in the task, or require two versions of the same message for different audiences.
Use a question-and-answer segment; responding to an unprepared question is where adaptation shows.
Where only one audience is ever addressed, record that limitation alongside the evidence rather than over-claiming the indicator.
rubric_criteria: Matches technical depth and terminology to the stated audience.
Responds to audience questions at an appropriate level.
PI33.attainment_methodology: Percentage of assessed students meeting the defined rubric level on the audience-adaptation criterion.
PI33.evidence_note: The hardest SO3 indicator to evidence from written work alone.

PI41.demonstrates: the student recognises the ethical and professional responsibilities present in an engineering situation
PI41.relationship: SO4 begins with recognition: before judgment can be assessed, the student has to see that a situation carries a professional or ethical obligation at all.
strengthening: Use a case or scenario in which the ethical dimension is not announced, so recognising it is the measured act.
Anchor the criterion to a named framework such as the IEEE Code of Ethics or the Saudi Council of Engineers Engineer's Charter, both of which the program already references.
rubric_criteria: Identifies the ethical or professional responsibilities raised by the situation.
Relates the situation to a recognised professional code or charter.
PI41.attainment_methodology: Percentage of assessed students meeting the defined rubric level on the ethical-recognition criterion of a nominated case task.
PI41.evidence_note: This indicator carries an ABET rubric in the program framework.

PI42.demonstrates: the student reaches a reasoned judgment that weighs global, societal, economic and environmental impact
PI42.relationship: PI42 completes SO4 by asking for a decision and its justification, not only for awareness of the issue.
strengthening: Require a stated decision with its reasoning, rather than a discussion that stops at listing considerations.
Score whether the impacts named actually bear on the decision taken.
rubric_criteria: States a defensible judgment for the situation.
Weighs global, societal, economic and environmental impact in reaching that judgment.
PI42.attainment_methodology: Percentage of assessed students meeting the defined rubric level on the informed-judgment criterion.
PI42.evidence_note: Pairs naturally with PI41 on the same case task, scored as two rubric rows.

PI51.demonstrates: the student contributes reliably to shared team tasks and objectives
PI51.relationship: SO5 is about observed behaviour inside a team, so the evidence has to come from something that watches the student work, not from the team's product.
strengthening: Add a short behaviour-anchored peer or instructor rating to the existing team activity; this is usually the smallest change that converts a team task into SO5 evidence.
Score the individual, not the team deliverable; a shared project mark cannot report this indicator.
rubric_criteria: Completes assigned team tasks on time and to the agreed standard.
Participates dependably in team meetings and shared decisions.
PI51.attainment_methodology: Percentage of assessed students meeting the defined rubric level on the contribution criterion of the team instrument.
PI51.evidence_note: This indicator carries an ABET rubric in the program framework and applies to both low-level and senior courses.

PI52.demonstrates: the student plans and manages shared work and supports a collaborative, inclusive team environment
PI52.relationship: PI52 is the leadership half of SO5; it needs a team task long enough for planning and coordination to become visible.
strengthening: Require a team plan with allocated roles and revisit it at a milestone; the revision is the evidence.
Include an inclusivity criterion phrased as observable behaviour rather than as attitude.
rubric_criteria: Plans and allocates team tasks and tracks them to completion.
Supports a collaborative and inclusive working environment.
PI52.attainment_methodology: Percentage of assessed students meeting the defined rubric level on the planning and team-environment criteria.
PI52.evidence_note: Program guidance places this indicator in senior courses with a design project.

PI61.demonstrates: the student develops an appropriate experiment rather than following a supplied procedure
PI61.relationship: SO6 starts with developing experimentation, which is the part a fully prescribed laboratory sheet cannot evidence.
strengthening: Include at least one open or partly open laboratory task where the procedure is designed by the student.
Score the experimental plan as a deliverable in its own right, before the data are collected.
rubric_criteria: Designs an experimental procedure capable of answering the stated question.
Selects appropriate instrumentation, ranges and controls.
PI61.attainment_methodology: Percentage of assessed students meeting the defined rubric level on the experiment-design criterion.
PI61.evidence_note: This indicator carries an ABET rubric in the program framework. Program guidance places it in senior courses that include experiment development.

PI62.demonstrates: the student runs the experiment and collects usable data
PI62.relationship: PI62 is the execution step of SO6 and is best observed while the student is at the bench.
strengthening: Use an observed practical checkpoint so setup and measurement technique are scored, not only the numbers submitted.
Keep the raw data record with the report; it is the evidence that the data were actually collected.
rubric_criteria: Sets up and operates the experiment correctly and safely.
Collects data that are complete, recorded and usable.
PI62.attainment_methodology: Percentage of assessed students meeting the defined rubric level on the data-collection criterion of an observed practical.
PI62.evidence_note: Simulation-only work can carry this indicator when the simulation is the experiment; state that decision explicitly.

PI63.demonstrates: the student analyses and interprets data, including uncertainty and unexpected results
PI63.relationship: PI63 sits between the data and the conclusion in SO6, and is the SO6 indicator that analysis-led courses carry most naturally.
strengthening: Score interpretation separately from computation: what the data mean, not only what they are.
Include a case where the data do not match theory, so the interpretation has real work to do.
rubric_criteria: Processes data correctly, including units, uncertainty and outliers.
Interprets what the data show in terms of the underlying engineering behaviour.
PI63.attainment_methodology: Percentage of assessed students meeting the defined rubric level on the data-analysis and interpretation criterion.
PI63.evidence_note: Frequently mapped across the program; nominate a small number of artifacts rather than aggregating everything.

PI64.demonstrates: the student uses engineering judgment to draw conclusions the data actually support
PI64.relationship: PI64 closes SO6. It is distinct from PI63 because it asks what should be concluded and what should not.
strengthening: Require an explicit conclusions section tied back to the original question, scored as its own criterion.
Ask for the limits of the conclusion; recognising what the data cannot support is strong evidence of judgment.
rubric_criteria: Draws conclusions that follow from the evidence presented.
States the limitations and the confidence attached to those conclusions.
PI64.attainment_methodology: Percentage of assessed students meeting the defined rubric level on the conclusions criterion.
PI64.evidence_note: Program guidance notes that this indicator should be reflected in the laboratory manuals.

PI71.demonstrates: the student locates and learns something not taught in the course, using a deliberate learning strategy
PI71.relationship: SO7 is about the process of learning, so the evidence has to show the gap the student started from and the route taken to close it.
strengthening: Require a short statement of what was not known, which sources were used and why they were trusted.
Set at least one task whose solution depends on a tool, standard or technique deliberately not covered in class.
rubric_criteria: Identifies the knowledge gap and selects credible sources to close it.
Describes the learning strategy used and evaluates its effectiveness.
PI71.attainment_methodology: Percentage of assessed students meeting the defined rubric level on the knowledge-acquisition criterion.
PI71.evidence_note: This indicator carries an ABET rubric in the program framework. Without a declared self-directed component the evidence is easy to assume and hard to show.

PI72.demonstrates: the student puts newly acquired knowledge to work on an engineering task
PI72.relationship: PI72 is what makes SO7 assessable as engineering rather than as study skills: the new knowledge has to change the work product.
strengthening: Score the application of the newly learned material, not the act of finding it.
Ask the student to point to where in the deliverable the new knowledge was used.
rubric_criteria: Applies the newly acquired knowledge correctly to the engineering task.
Shows that the result depended on the newly acquired knowledge.
PI72.attainment_methodology: Percentage of assessed students meeting the defined rubric level on the applied-knowledge criterion.
PI72.evidence_note: Pairs naturally with PI71 on the same deliverable, scored as two rubric rows.

so_evidence_notes.SO1: Analysis evidence is abundant across the program. The useful work here is narrowing to nominated items rather than finding more coverage.
so_evidence_notes.SO2: Design evidence is strongest where a specification and a produced solution are both present. Analysis-led courses can carry SO2 well when a task is framed against stated specifications.
so_evidence_notes.SO3: Communication evidence depends on keeping the graded artifact and a criterion-level rubric, not only the mark.
so_evidence_notes.SO4: Ethical recognition and judgment need a case or a decision point. The program already carries the IEEE Code of Ethics and the Saudi Council of Engineers Engineer's Charter as reference frameworks.
so_evidence_notes.SO5: Teamwork evidence has to observe the individual inside the team; a shared deliverable mark cannot report it.
so_evidence_notes.SO6: Experimentation evidence is strongest where the laboratory work is at least partly open and the conclusions section is scored separately.
so_evidence_notes.SO7: Self-directed learning evidence needs a declared component that is deliberately not taught in class.

measurement_layer.policy: No student performance or attainment value is stored or generated by this module. When real assessment data are connected they populate the records array below, and the page will show measured attainment beside the alignment analysis rather than in place of it.

record_schema.artifact_id: string, identifier of the assessment artifact
record_schema.term: string, matching the assessment plan term identifier
record_schema.rubric_criterion_id: string, identifier of the scored criterion
record_schema.sample_size: integer, number of students in the assessed sample
record_schema.threshold: object, the faculty-defined rubric level counted as meeting the indicator
record_schema.attainment_percent: number, derived from the two counts above and never entered by hand
record_schema.evidence_mode: string, one of direct, direct_observational, external_observational, indirect

improvement_layer.policy: Findings, improvement actions and reassessment results are recorded only after real measurement data exist. Nothing in this release generates them.

record_schema.finding: string, what the measured attainment showed
record_schema.action: string, the improvement action agreed by the committee

analysis_scope.label: Analysis scope: Core curriculum
analysis_scope.statement: Program-level conclusions are based on required courses only, because they represent the curriculum experienced by every EE student. Elective courses are shown separately for exploration and are not included in guaranteed program-coverage judgments.
analysis_scope.elective_note: Electives are not less important; they answer a different curriculum question. A student takes only a subset of the elective pool, so elective mappings describe enrichment opportunities rather than coverage every graduate is guaranteed to experience.

dimension_model.intro: A single status answers several questions at once. These three dimensions keep them apart, so that a conceptual judgment is never confused with a documentation gap.

conceptual_alignment.label: Conceptual Alignment
conceptual_alignment.question: Does the CLO reasonably support this Performance Indicator?
conceptual_alignment.source: Read from the outcome statement against the demonstration the indicator describes.

primary.label: Directly aligned
primary.description: The statement asks for the same kind of demonstration the indicator describes.

supporting.label: Supporting alignment
supporting.description: The statement supports the indicator through a related demonstration - a normal arrangement where one task carries several outcomes.

unclear.label: Wording not explicit
unclear.description: The statement carries no distinct demonstration verb, so the mapping rests on the design of the assessed task rather than on the wording. This is a wording observation, not a mapping concern.

distant.label: Worth a closer look
distant.description: The statement describes a noticeably different kind of demonstration from the indicator. The preserve path is offered first in every case.

evidence_readiness.label: Evidence Readiness
evidence_readiness.question: Do the assessment methods already declared for this CLO provide a suitable potential carrier for this indicator?
evidence_readiness.source: Declared assessment methods in the approved curriculum, matched against the artifact types that normally carry the indicator.
evidence_readiness.caution: A declared assessment method means a suitable evidence opportunity exists. It does not mean the indicator has been measured.

strong.label: Preferred carrier declared
strong.description: An artifact type normally used to report this indicator is already among the declared methods.

partial.label: Supporting carrier declared
partial.description: A related artifact type is declared. It can support the mapping; the preferred carrier would report it more directly.

limited.label: Carrier not yet named
limited.description: None of the declared methods is an artifact type normally used to report this indicator. The mapping stands; the evidence route for it is not yet named.

evidence_specificity.label: Evidence Specificity
evidence_specificity.question: Has an actual assessment artifact and a PI-specific rubric criterion been identified for this mapping?
evidence_specificity.source: The Evidence and Measurement layers. No artifact has been linked in this release, so this dimension reports what is recommended rather than what has been recorded.
evidence_specificity.caution: This is the dimension that turns an evidence opportunity into defensible attainment evidence. It is intentionally unfilled until real artifacts are connected.

documented.label: Artifact documented
documented.description: A specific artifact and rubric criterion are recorded against this mapping.

recommended.label: Recommended, not yet documented
recommended.description: The page proposes a suitable artifact type and rubric criterion. Nothing has been linked yet, so the indicator has not been shown to be measured.

not_available.label: No recommendation available
not_available.description: No evidence profile exists for this indicator yet.

program_conclusion.intro: The headline conclusion is derived from the core-curriculum analysis using the thresholds below. It is a descriptive summary of the current mapping and its evidence opportunities, not an attainment judgment.

tiers.headline: Strong and broadly defensible
tiers.summary: Across the required curriculum, the great majority of CLO to PI relationships read as well supported or defensible, every Student Outcome is represented, and only a small number of relationships show enough conceptual distance to merit a faculty conversation. The productive work here is sharpening evidence rather than revisiting the mapping.
tiers.plain_headline: Core curriculum alignment appears strong and broadly defensible.

tiers.headline: Broadly defensible, with focused opportunities to strengthen evidence
tiers.summary: Most relationships in the required curriculum read as well supported or defensible. An identifiable group would be easier to defend with a clearer evidence route or a PI-specific rubric criterion.
tiers.plain_headline: Core curriculum alignment appears broadly defensible.

tiers.headline: Defensible overall, with several areas where evidence could be strengthened
tiers.summary: The mapping holds across the required curriculum. Several outcomes would benefit from a clearer evidence route before their attainment is reported.
tiers.plain_headline: Core curriculum alignment appears defensible, with some areas to strengthen.

tiers.headline: Mapping is in place; evidence documentation is the main area to develop
tiers.summary: The approved mapping covers the required curriculum. The clearest next step is naming the artifacts and rubric criteria that would carry the evidence.
tiers.plain_headline: The required curriculum is fully mapped; the evidence behind it is still being documented.

so_next_steps.SO1: Choose a small number of nominated items rather than aggregating whole papers, so reported attainment traces back to one indicator at a time.
so_next_steps.SO2: Confirm that the design-led courses carrying most of these relationships use criterion-level rubric rows, so the design, constraints and standards indicators can be reported separately.
so_next_steps.SO3: Keep the graded report or presentation itself, not only the mark, and name content, representation and audience adaptation as separate rubric rows.
so_next_steps.SO4: Nominate one case or decision task in a core course as the ethics evidence point, and anchor its criterion to the IEEE Code of Ethics or the Saudi Council of Engineers Engineer’s Charter that the program already references.
so_next_steps.SO5: Add a short behaviour-anchored peer or instructor rating to the team activities that already exist. This is usually the smallest change that turns a team task into individual SO5 evidence, because a shared project mark cannot report it.
so_next_steps.SO6: Ensure the nominated artifacts score experiment development, data interpretation and conclusions as separate criteria rather than as one laboratory mark.
so_next_steps.SO7: Declare which component of the course is deliberately not taught in class, so the self-directed learning step is visible in the artifact rather than assumed.

future_modules.name: Elective Pool Consistency Analysis
future_modules.rationale: Electives are excluded from guaranteed core-program coverage because a student selects only part of the elective pool. Two students can complete the same degree through very different elective paths.
questions: Do different permitted elective choices provide reasonably balanced Student Outcome and Performance Indicator opportunities?
Does the elective pool contain unintended gaps, where some outcomes are reachable only through a few electives?
Does evidence quality vary significantly depending on which electives a student takes?
Do the permitted elective combinations maintain the intended educational experience?
future_modules.note: Not implemented in this release. The elective mappings are already analysed and can be inspected through the exploration tools on this page; only the combination-level analysis is deferred.

so_short_checks.SO1: Nominate specific exam or assignment items rather than whole papers.
so_short_checks.SO2: Confirm the design courses score design, constraints and standards as separate rubric rows.
so_short_checks.SO3: Keep the graded report or presentation, not only the mark.
so_short_checks.SO4: Confirm the CLO–PI relationships involving ethical and professional responsibility.
so_short_checks.SO5: Confirm that at least one nominated team activity evaluates individual contribution.
so_short_checks.SO6: Score experiment design, data interpretation and conclusions separately.
so_short_checks.SO7: Make the self-directed-learning component explicit in the nominated evidence.
